entries.04be902424cbbe25: This business operates discount stores and supermarkets in Hawaii and California in the United States. The main companies are Don Quijote (USA) Co., Ltd., Gelson's Markets, MARUKAI CORPORATION and QSI, Inc. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended June 2026 was ¥277,936 million (up 7.1% year on year), increasing due to new store openings in California, the consolidation of Mikuni Restaurant Group, Inc. as a subsidiary, and the effect of exchange rates. On the other hand, the destruction of stores by wildfires and the closure of unprofitable stores were factors that reduced revenue. Stores opened during the period were four in California, USA (TOKYO CENTRAL Irvine, TOKYO CENTRAL Emeryville, Gelson's Toluca Lake, and the sushi restaurant El Dorado Hills), and one store was closed.
entries.070aacc1f0dd8a0f: In August 2025, the company formulated a new long-term management plan, "Double Impact 2035," and sets a target of ¥4.2 trillion in revenue for the fiscal year ended June 2035. There are five growth policies: a store-opening strategy (aiming to expand market share by filling blank areas with no stores yet, as store openings advance in every prefecture); an existing-store strategy (aiming for substantial growth in top-line sales by creating reasons to visit for the "passive avoidance group"); an inbound strategy (aiming to establish "tourist-destination-style retail"); development of new formats (food-focused Donki stores based on "(Donki's editing capability + UNY's fresh food procurement capability) × discount"); and an M&A strategy (taking M&A as one of its strategies in anticipation of reorganization and oligopolization in the retail industry). For the fiscal year ending June 2027, the company states it will advance revitalization of Olympic Group stores and accelerate store openings in Japan.

entries.400ec05e65cfd7d3: This business operates "DON DON DONKI" stores in Asia, built on the concept of a Japan-brand specialty store. The main companies are Pan Pacific Retail Management(Singapore) Pte.Ltd. and Pan Pacific Retail Management(Hong Kong) Co.,Ltd. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended June 2026 was ¥99,129 million (up 8.7% from the previous year). The company gives as the reasons for the increase in revenue that it reviewed the product mix (MD composition) in each area, launched new products, expanded assortments and strengthened product procurement using local distribution channels, which raised price competitiveness and increased the number of customers. In this fiscal year, 1 store opened in the Kingdom of Thailand (DON DON DONKI Central Westgate store), and 5 stores closed.

entries.62280c4b65d1606d: Consolidated revenue for the fiscal year ended June 2026 was ¥2,445,260 million (up 8.8% year on year; ¥2,246,758 million in the previous fiscal year), and it has increased every year since the fiscal year ended June 2022. Revenue from external customers by reportable [[term:segment|segment]] was ¥2,068,195 million for the Domestic Business (up 9.1% year on year), ¥277,936 million for the North America Business (up 7.1%) and ¥99,129 million for the Asia Business (up 8.7%), with the Domestic Business the largest. The breakdown of Domestic Business sales results is discount stores ¥1,505,328 million (up 7.8% year on year), UNY Business ¥449,776 million (up 5.5%) and other revenue ¥113,092 million (153.1% year on year), and the contents of "other revenue" are not printed. The reasons the company gives for the revenue increase in the Domestic Business are: a rise in customer traffic at existing stores from pricing strategies and sales promotions responding to changes in customer behavior, strong performance of IP content products and trend products, a record high in duty-free sales, and 25 new store openings. In the North America Business, revenue increased due to new store openings in California, Mikuni Restaurant Group, Inc. becoming a consolidated subsidiary, and the effect of exchange rates, while store losses from wildfires and closures of unprofitable stores were factors that decreased revenue. In the Asia Business, the company reviewed product mix (MD composition) in each area and strengthened procurement using local distribution channels, which raised price competitiveness and increased customer traffic.

entries.9f56ec9d17f21061: It condenses the purchase motives customers look for in retail into 3 points, "more convenient (CV)," "cheaper (D)" and "more fun (A)," and has made "CV＋D＋A" its business concept. It holds that convenience and low prices alone stop at "1+1=2," and that "amusement," which creates the added value of "excitement and thrills," is what leads to "1+1=∞," and says it uses this to differentiate itself from other retailers. It also cites as a differentiating factor from competitors its strengths based on a field-first, store-by-store approach.

entries.d4535fa1b0554f6a: In Japan, this is the largest of the three reportable segments, operating the big convenience and discount store "Don Quijote," the family-oriented general discount stores "MEGA Don Quijote" and "MEGA Don Quijote UNY," and the general supermarkets "Apita" and "Piago." Don Quijote Co., Ltd., Nagasakiya Co., Ltd. and UD Retail Co., Ltd. operate "Don Quijote" and other stores in chain nationwide, and UNY Co., Ltd. runs a general retail business covering clothing, food, housing and leisure. In addition, Kanebi Foods Co., Ltd. handles retail of sushi, fried foods and prepared dishes and manufactures and sells lunch boxes for convenience stores; Pan Pacific International Financial Services Co., Ltd. and UCS Co., Ltd. handle credit card, electronic money and insurance agency businesses; and Acreative Co., Ltd. provides financial services including early purchase of accounts receivable. Nihon Asset Marketing Co., Ltd. leases and manages commercial properties for the group's discount store companies, and Nihon Shogyo Shisetsu Co., Ltd. leases and manages tenants in mixed-use commercial facilities. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended June 2026 was ¥2,068,195 million (up 9.1% year on year). The company cites as reasons for the revenue increase: the growth in customer numbers at existing stores from pricing strategies and sales promotions adapted to changes in customer behavior; strong sales of IP content products and trend products that appeal to customers' tastes; a rise in customers from Southeast Asia, Europe and the United States that brought tax-exempt sales to a record high; and 25 new store openings. The new food-focused format "Kyoraku no Denden Robin Hood" opened its first store in April 2026, and had five stores by June 2026. The number of domestic stores at the end of June 2026 was 676, and during the period four stores in Japan were closed. In the sales table, "other revenue" of ¥113,092 million (up 153.1% year on year) is included in the domestic business, in addition to the discount store and UNY businesses.

entries.ecffa0a2368f3761: Customers are mainly individuals visiting stores, and revenue by customer location is ¥2,068,195 million in Japan, ¥277,936 million in the U.S. and ¥99,129 million in Asia (fiscal year ended June 2026). In Japan, "MEGA Don Quijote" and "MEGA Don Quijote UNY" are family-oriented stores. entries.f69146a7a6f7c8fd: In Japan, it operates discount-format stores such as "Don Quijote," "MEGA Don Quijote" and "MEGA Don Quijote UNY," and general merchandise stores such as "Apita" and "Piago." Its products include food, daily necessities, watches and fashion items, sports and leisure goods, and home appliances. The company sees the purchase motives customers look for in retail as 3 points, "more convenient," "cheaper" and "more fun," and from their initials sets out its business concept as "CV＋D＋A." In April 2026 it opened the first store of a new food-focused format, "Kyoraku no Dendo Robin Hood," and by June 2026 it had 5 stores. The number of stores at the end of June 2026 was 676 in Japan and 123 overseas, 799 in total (779 stores at the end of June 2025). In North America it operates discount stores, supermarkets and other stores in Hawaii and California, and in Asia it operates "DON DON DONKI." In addition, it provides financial services such as credit cards, electronic money and insurance agency, leases commercial properties and tenant space, and manufactures and sells boxed meals for convenience stores.
